subject: Recap & next steps — procurement path and payment method
messages:
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gonzalez <m.gonzalez@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 12 Mar 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Recap & next steps — procurement path and payment method

Hi Maria — thanks again for making time today. Quick recap from our discovery and clear next steps so we can move toward a POC/pilot.

Call recap:
- Use case: real-time document ingestion + retrieval-augmented generation for compliance workflows.
- Expected 6-12 month runway; pilot targets ~3k queries/day.
- Success criteria: <300ms 95th latency, < $0.004/token, and integration with your IAM.

Procurement & payment items we discussed (action items in bold):
- Preferred commercial path: PO (enterprise) vs corporate card (pilot). Please confirm which AP route you prefer for initial pilot.
- Marketplace interest: you mentioned exploring AWS Marketplace to simplify vendor onboarding — can you confirm if that’s a hard requirement or just preferred?
- Vendor onboarding docs: AP typically needs W-9 and SOC 2; procurement may require an onboarding form. Can you share your supplier onboarding template or procurement contact?
- Billing cadence: confirm whether Net-30 on PO would work for this account (we can support Net-30 for enterprise POs).

Next steps I propose:
1) You confirm AP preference (PO vs card) and share procurement contact and PO template.
2) If PO: send to procure@fintechcorp.com and cc me; we’ll return vendor onboarding materials filled and W-9/SOC2.
3) If marketplace: we’ll prepare a SKU list and short doc on how marketplace purchase shows up on your billing.

If helpful, I can prefill our onboarding form with high-level info and attach it — will do that in a follow-up.

Thanks — Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
rishi_malhotra@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0132
Redwood Inference
From: Maria Gonzalez <m.gonzalez@fintechcorp.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@fintechcorp.com
Date: Fri, 13 Mar 2026 10:01:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — procurement path and payment method

Thanks for the clear summary, Rishi. A few notes from AP/procurement side: 

- Vendor onboarding: Procurement requires our vendor onboarding form (attached) completed, plus a current SOC 2 report and W-9. I’ve attached the onboarding form (vendor_onboarding_template.docx).
- Payment policy: Our AP policy prefers POs for any commitment > $5,000. For pilots under $5k we can use a corporate card but it must be charged to a pre-approved cost center. PO terms: we typically accept Net-30 for named vendors after legal review.
- Marketplace: purchasing via AWS Marketplace is preferred because it bypasses some internal vendor onboarding steps, but legal still needs to review EULAs. If Redwood has a marketplace listing, please send SKUs and any Marketplace-specific SLAs/pricing.

Question: can Redwood accept a Net-30 on a PO for this pilot if we commit to ramp by quarter end? Also — who on your side owns vendor onboarding (contact for the supplier pack)?

procure@fintechcorp.com: I’m copying procurement so they have visibility and can flag any missing items.

Thanks,
Maria Gonzalez
Head of Procurement, FinTechCorp
m.gonzalez@fintechcorp.com
From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Maria Gonzalez <m.gonzalez@fintechcorp.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 14 Mar 2026 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — procurement path and payment method

Hi Maria — appreciate the details and for looping in procurement. A couple quick answers and attached artifacts to speed things up.

- Net-30: yes, Redwood can accept Net-30 on a PO for enterprise accounts (we’ll route to finance + legal for the standard SOW/invoice flow).
- Marketplace: we do have a listing in AWS Marketplace; purchasing there will typically reduce vendor onboarding friction. I attached a one-pager that explains how charges appear and the SKU list.
- Vendor onboarding owner: Laura Bennett (cc’d) owns supplier/onboarding and will coordinate documents with your team.

Attachments:
- redwood-marketplace-integration.pdf (one-pager with SKUs + how billing shows up)
- vendor-onboarding-form-filled.docx (pre-filled version of your template with high-level company info)

Next steps (proposed):
1) Procurement: if you send a PO to procure@fintechcorp.com (cc me + laura_bennett@redwood.com), we’ll acknowledge within 24 business hours and open a supplier ticket.
2) If you prefer marketplace: let us know which SKUs you want and we’ll prepare a quote and expected on-cloud billing cadence.
3) Legal/Compliance: I will attach SOC 2 + W-9 in the same ticket.

If useful, we can schedule a short call Monday to run through the onboarding checklist with procurement.

Thanks — Rishi

--
Rishi Malhotra
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
From: Maria Gonzalez <m.gonzalez@fintechcorp.com>
To: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
Cc: procure@fintechcorp.com
Date: Sun, 15 Mar 2026 09:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Recap & next steps — procurement path and payment method

Thanks — confirmed. Procurement will route a PO for the pilot (expected to be under the $5k threshold) but we’d prefer to buy via AWS Marketplace if your SKUs/pricing match the pilot scope — fewer forms for us.

Action items on our side:
- Procurement: will create and route PO to procure@fintechcorp.com by EOD Tue and will include preferred cost center.
- Procurement: please provide marketplace SKUs and the quick one-pager you mentioned so we can compare.
- Compliance: we still need your SOC 2 report and W-9; please attach in the supplier ticket.

procure@fintechcorp.com: please coordinate next steps; we want to minimize vendor onboarding where possible and use marketplace purchase if it simplifies billing.

On copy: Laura, can you confirm receipt of the vendor_onboarding_form_filled and SOC2/W-9 when you open the supplier ticket?

Best,
Maria
